title: damagedCronJob Studios page: choose the visual world
question: The roll dealt the toy aisle. Keep it, take the level-select map, or re-roll.

options.label: The Toy Aisle Pegboard
options.lineage: blister-packed toys hanging on a shop's pegboard wall
options.thesis: Every title hangs on the studio's pegboard like a toy in its blister pack: pick one off the wall.
options.viewport: A warm pegboard wall fills the screen: the studio's header card hangs top left, four packs hang on pegs, Magnet Mob's the biggest with its App Store button printed on the card.
options.risk: Becomes a toy-shop costume if the packs are flat rectangles; the blister, hang tab and printing must be crafted, and press facts must stay readable.

raised.raise: Packs hang on real pegs with pendulum physics: they swing when the pointer brushes them and settle.
The pegboard's hole pitch is the page's only grid; every pack, label and gap snaps to it, phones included.
One shout per card: each title set big and angled like toy-box lettering, loudness ranked by what the card sells.
Every card is its own composition, and a tap flips it once, completely, to a printed back with the facts and links.
Status (Out now, Android soon) is printed on the card as stickers, never as UI badges.
Only real facts sit in fixed positions: platform and release date on each pack's price-tag strip.

options.label: Level Select
options.lineage: the overworld map of a platform game
options.thesis: The studio as a game's level-select map: each title is a world on one winding path.
options.viewport: A bright overworld fills the screen; the path runs from the studio's start flag through four title worlds, Magnet Mob's node marked NEW with its Play button.
options.risk: The most familiar game-studio trope after a card grid; it needs real illustration craft or it reads as clip art.

options.label: ASCII Live Scene
options.thesis: Each title rendered live in monospace glyphs, density standing in for light.
options.viewport: Magnet Mob's army running in glyphs across a phosphor grid, the studio name typed above.
options.case: Fits the programmer joke but hides the games behind text, and it is the cron and terminal rut the owner rejected.
options.kept: One strict grid as the whole composition.
options.risk: Reads as a terminal costume; players can't see the games.

options.label: Matchbook Drawer
options.thesis: Each title as a collected matchbook cover that flips open for details.
options.viewport: A drawer of four covers fanned in the hand, Magnet Mob's on top.
options.case: A collectible object world, but nightlife ephemera doesn't say games; the toys do.
options.kept: One cover, one composition; single complete flips.
options.risk: Nostalgic mood with no play in it.

options.label: Futurist Bolted Book
options.thesis: The studio as a loud bolted book, each title a slamming spread.
options.viewport: A spread with DAMAGED CRON JOB slammed diagonally across it.
options.case: Loud and bold but avant-garde print, far from a player's world.

options.label: Gravity Rain Garden
options.thesis: Titles as objects in a garden where coloured rains fall by their own gravity.
options.viewport: A dusk garden with four title objects caught in different rains.
options.case: A beautiful toy, but neither players nor press would recognise a studio in it.
options.kept: A real physical law governing interaction.
options.risk: A demo, not a studio page.

options.label: Chromatophore Skin
options.lineage: cephalopod skin as a living display
options.thesis: The page as living skin whose patterns signal each title.
options.viewport: A pale skin field rippling into four title patterns.
options.case: No link to games or to the studio's name.
options.kept: State drawn onto the surface itself.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Studio facts glowing in nixie tubes.
options.viewport: A bank of tubes counting up the studio's titles.
options.case: The page has almost no real numbers to show, and claims are off the table.
options.risk: An instrument costume with nothing to count.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark hero with the studio logo over a grid of game key-art cards, then about and contact.
canonCard.viewport: Logo and one line up top, four game cards below, each with a store button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every studio site by design.
